findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - saving either screen picture after the target page loads.
The stand-in now evaluates the readiness expression, but its screenshot is still fabricated: it appends the page's HTML to a 24-byte buffer rather than rendering a PNG. The assertions at lines 91–95 therefore do not show that either saved picture contains the page. For example, a regression that asks Chrome to capture an empty area would pass because the stand-in ignores screenshot parameters and returns the HTML anyway. The existing real-browser viewport test checks dimensions, not page content.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_renderer_waits_for_the_page_to_load

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - running the platform-sensitive suite on Windows.
The Windows skip avoids the original process-launch failure, but both cases of the renderer regression test are still never executable there. The Windows workflow selects the platform-marked file and then skips both cases, so it cannot detect the blank-page race on this supported platform. The existing real-browser viewport test checks image dimensions and overflow, not the delayed navigation case.
findings.title: Keep the renderer regression test executable on Windows

why: Bug 1507. The renderer can measure and save the empty first page (about:blank) as the design screen, so a saved picture can be blank while the phone width check still passes.
